correctness.rationale: The parity decomposition of hyperbinary expansions gives the polynomial recurrence for all positive indices; the two pair transitions are algebraically derived in Z[zeta_5]. The attached exact table has 120 distinct integral states, contains (zeta_5,1), is closed under both transformations at every state (240 transitions), and every first-coordinate cyclotomic coefficient vector has range at most two after adjoining zero. Binary-index induction places every evaluation pair in this table. Coordinate uniqueness identifies the vector as (C0-C4,...,C3-C4), proving the all-index bound. The independent coefficient recurrence checks indices 0..12000; H_10=z^2+2z^3+z^4+z^5 proves sharpness. The published fence rank correspondence transports the bound via cyclic shifts and reflections of residues; the empty fence is handled separately.

originality.rationale: Relevant full-text sections and claim-level semantic comparisons reveal only the modulo-three discrepancy theorem, the basic hyperbinary/fence polynomial identity, and third/fourth-root rational q-polynomial restrictions. None of the inspected claims yields the sharp modulo-five discrepancy or the exact 120-state certificate. The modular-five assertion is not implied by residue-three balance, and the mere general generating-function identity does not bound fifth-root evaluations. Historical priority remains provisional.
